 Follow Powerball numbers drawn: Did anyone win $674 million?
 Fernando Cervantes Jr., USA TODAY Updated Sun, October 25, 2026 at 1:00 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The numbers are in for Saturday night's $674 million Powerball drawing . Now comes the big question: Did anyone win the jackpot?
 A winner has yet to be announced for the Oct. 24 drawing, which carried a $289.1 million cash option. The jackpot has been growing since a player in Illinois won an estimated $1.04 billion on Aug. 12.
 Here's what to know about Saturday night's Powerball drawing.

 When is the next Powerball drawing?
 The next Powerball drawing will take place on Monday, October 26, at 10:59 p.m. ET. The drawing can be watched live on Powerball's website , and players can rewatch clips on its YouTube channel .
 Powerball drawings occur every week on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday.

 How to play Powerball
 Powerball tickets cost $2 per play and are sold in 45 states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Depending on local laws, players may also be able to purchase tickets online.
 Advertisement Advertisement To play, select five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26. Players can also add Power Play for an extra $1 to boost non-jackpot prizes by 2X, 3X, 4X, 5X or 10X.
 Prefer to leave it to chance? Choose a Quick Pick and let the computer generate your numbers.
 To win the jackpot, a ticket must match all five white balls and the red Powerball. If no one wins, the jackpot rolls over and continues to grow.
 Do you have to be a U.S. citizen or resident to play Powerball?
 You do not have to be a U.S. citizen or resident to buy a Powerball ticket.
 Anyone who meets the legal age requirement where the ticket is purchased, generally 18 or older, can play while visiting a participating jurisdiction. Winners who live outside the United States are eligible to claim prizes, although taxes may apply.
